Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the failing test checks:
  - BugCLI266Test.testOptionComparatorInsertedOrder() builds an Options instance with a specific insertion sequence of short options: first a standalone “h”, then options via two OptionGroups (“d”, “f” in the first; “x”, “s”, “p” in the second), and finally “t”, “w”, “o”. It then iterates over getOptions().getOptions() and asserts that each Option’s short name (o.getOpt()) matches an expected insertedOrder list.
- How Options currently returns options:
  - Options.getOptions() returns Collections.unmodifiableCollection(helpOptions()).
  - Options.helpOptions() constructs a new ArrayList from shortOpts.values().
- Why this breaks insertion order:
  - The order of elements returned by Map.values() depends entirely on the Map implementation. If shortOpts is a plain HashMap (or any non-order-preserving map), the iteration order of values is not the insertion order. Therefore, helpOptions() does not preserve the order in which options were added.
  - As a result, testOptionComparatorInsertedOrder() observes options in a non-deterministic order and fails when comparing to the expected insertedOrder.
- Relation to the bug report:
  - The report states that HelpFormatter#setOptionComparator(null) does not display options in insertion order. When the comparator is null, HelpFormatter relies on the order provided by Options.getOptions(). Since getOptions() (via helpOptions()) pulls from shortOpts.values() without guaranteed insertion order, HelpFormatter also outputs options in an arbitrary order, matching the reported behavior.
- Conclusion:
  - The root cause is that Options.helpOptions() builds its list from a map (shortOpts) whose iteration order does not preserve insertion order. This loses the order in which options and option-group members were added, causing both the failing test and the reported HelpFormatter behavior. The fix is to ensure that option storage preserves insertion order (e.g., by using a LinkedHashMap for shortOpts and related structures) or to explicitly maintain and return a list in insertion order.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
